QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_31

question.text: The Logic Model / LFM discipline taught in Ch 4 of the SIA workbook MOST directly supports which SEBI-mandated SSE disclosure?

answer.text: The Annual Impact Report (AIR) required from SSE-listed entities, which relies on indicator-level evidence and MoV for the SIA's assurance opinion
The audited financial statements under Section 134 of the Companies Act
Form 10B income tax return for trusts

explanation.text: The Logic: The AIR is the SSE-listed entity's annual disclosure of social outputs/outcomes/impact, audited/assured by the empanelled SIA. The AIR depends directly on a sound LFM (indicator hierarchy, OVI, MoV, assumption disclosure) — the Logic Model discipline IS the foundation of the AIR. The other three are separate statutory filings under Companies Act, Income Tax Act and FCRA respectively. The Trap: B, C, D are all statutory filings with separate regimes — candidates must not conflate them with SSE impact disclosure. Cross-Exam Context: Tested extensively in XXIII Ch 7 (SAS-100 assurance) and cross-referenced in III-A / III-C Compliance (listed-entity disclosure) and XXIV / IFSCA-01 AML (FCRA overlap). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Build your AIR engagement work-paper tree around the LFM rows. Each row gets a folder: indicator, target, MoV, evidence, tick-mark, observation. If a row has no folder, you have no audit trail.
